analysis.hypothesis: Implement three separate CUDA kernels and their launchers: reflection_pad2d, relu, and index_select (full-range identity). Each launcher will be exported as extern "C" for binding layer. ReflectionPad2d needs to handle padding with reflection without accessing out-of-bounds. ReLU is elementwise. Index_select with None index defaults to full range along given dimension, which is identity operation but must copy tensor to a new allocation to satisfy semantics (though model returns the same tensor shape). All kernels must work on contiguous float32 CUDA tensors, with grid-stride loops.
evidence: model_new.py calls cuda_extension.reflection_pad2d_forward(x, self.kernel_size), cuda_extension.relu_forward(x), cuda_extension.index_select_forward(x, self.dim, None).
Task contract shows input shape [512,3,170,170], output [512,3,176,176] after pad, and index_select should be identity because indices are full range along dim 0.
Only float32 tensors are used; all inputs are contiguous as per get_inputs.
Binding layer will be created in a separate stage; launchers must have C linkage and accept raw pointers, dimensions, and stream.

analysis.hypothesis: The custom_ops.cu already exports three launchers: reflection_pad2d_launcher, relu_launcher, index_select_launcher. A binding.cpp is required to wrap these launchers with PyTorch tensor checks, allocation, stream retrieval, and pybind registration. The binding will define three Python functions: reflection_pad2d_forward, relu_forward, index_select_forward, matching the calls in model_new.py.
